grammar_focus: 独立主格结构(名词 + 分词/形容词作状语)、现在分词短语作方式/伴随状语、it 作形式主语 + 不定式、情态动词 + 完成式(must have done 对过去推测 / should have done 本该做而未做)、with 复合结构/either…or/短语动词(NCE3 第三册 Unit 3 无 KS 页,考点由课文结构 + Notes on the text 自取;原创承载·老太太回家发现公寓被窃贼翻箱倒柜洗劫、报警找楼管的冷幽默悬疑·窃贼已逃无对峙无暴力;美语化 apartment/elevator/jewelry/master key)
scene: 老太太回到自己居住的公寓楼,心里很高兴。去店里买东西把她累坏了,回家路上每走一步,手里的袋子就更沉一点。在电梯里,她一心想着午饭和好好歇一歇;可当她在自家那层走出电梯,这两件事全被忘到脑后——她突然发现自家大门开着。她本想着第二天上午一定要好好说说那个钟点工,竟这么粗心大意;转念却记起,自己是钟点工走后才去买东西的,而且两把锁都是她亲手拧上的。她慢慢走进门厅,一眼就看见所有房门都敞着——可按照惯例,她出门前明明把它们都关好了。朝起居室望去,她看见写字台那边一片狼藉。事情十分清楚:她不在时,有窃贼闯了进来。她的第一反应是挨个房间去找那入侵者,但又觉得以自己这年纪,有人陪着也许更稳妥,于是下楼去地下室把楼管请了上来。这时她两腿已开始发抖,便坐下喝了一杯很浓的茶,楼管则给警察打了电话。镇定重新恢复后,她准备好和楼管一起动身,去搜查公寓里可能还潜藏着的人。他俩逐屋查看,小心翼翼不碰任何东西,生怕妨碍警察寻找指纹。屋里的混乱几乎叫人难以想象。她在这套公寓里住了三十年,又特别爱收藏东西;看上去她所有的家当都被翻了出来,里里外外倒腾了个遍。至少,她想,那些几年前就该扔掉的东西,如今倒省事了。随后一位巡官带着一名警员赶到,她讲了自己如何发现被洗劫的公寓。巡官开始找指纹,警员则查看大门锁并未被撬——由此证明,窃贼要么用了万能钥匙,要么是翻阳台进来的。指纹一无所获,巡官却发现一个脏兮兮的红布包,里头装着珠宝,老太太说那不是她的。看来这套公寓并不是窃贼当天下手的第一家,他一定是被惊扰了。巡官劝她这几夜别独自住,老太太觉得他大惊小怪,但既然楼管也附和,她便打电话给女儿求援,说自己碰上了一点儿小麻烦。

grammar_card.title: 独立主格 / 现在分词作状语 / it 形式主语 / 情态 + 完成式
grammar_card.intro: ①独立主格:名词(代词)+ 分词/形容词,作状语,有自己的逻辑主语:Her composure regained, she was ready…。②现在分词短语作方式/伴随状语,逻辑主语与主句一致:Looking into the room, she saw…;being careful to touch nothing。③it 作形式主语,真正主语是后面的不定式:It might be more prudent to have someone with her。④情态 + have + 过去分词:must have done(对过去推测“一定…了”)/ should have done(过去本该做而没做)。

rows: Looking into the room, she saw…
It might be prudent to have help

specialRules.rule: 独立主格有自己的逻辑主语(Her composure regained),不同于普通分词状语(逻辑主语=主句主语)。
must have done=对过去的肯定推测;should have done=过去本该做却没做,含责备/惋惜。
specialRules.mark: must have done / should have done

specialRules.rule: 美式用词:apartment(公寓,英式 flat)、elevator(电梯,英式 lift)、jewelry(珠宝,英式 jewellery)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What did the old lady find when she got home?
options: Her apartment had been broken into

passage: The old lady was glad to be back at the apartment building where she lived. Her shopping had tired her, and her bag had grown heavier with every step of the way home. In the elevator her thoughts were on lunch and a good rest; but when she stepped out at her own floor, both were forgotten in her sudden discovery that her front door stood open. She was thinking that she must reprimand her cleaning lady the next morning for such a careless piece of negligence, when she remembered that she had gone shopping after the cleaning lady had left, and she knew that she had turned both keys in their locks herself. She walked slowly into the hall and at once noticed that all the room doors were open, yet, following her regular habit, she had shut them before going out. Looking into the living room, she saw a scene of confusion over by her writing desk. It was as clear as daylight then that a burglar had forced an entry while she was away. Her first impulse was to go from room to room in search of the intruder, but she decided that, at her age, it might be more prudent to have someone with her. So she went down to fetch the building manager from the basement. By this time her legs were beginning to tremble, so she sat down and accepted a cup of very strong tea while he called the police. Then, her composure regained, she was ready to set off with the manager's help to look for anyone who might still be lurking in her apartment. They went through the rooms, being careful to touch nothing, as they did not want to hinder the police in their search for fingerprints. The chaos was almost inconceivable. She had lived in the apartment for thirty years and loved to collect and keep things; and it seemed as though everything she owned had been pulled out and turned over and over. At least, she thought, sorting out the things she should have discarded years ago was now being made easier for her. Then a police inspector arrived with an officer, and she told them how she had found the ransacked apartment. The inspector began to look for fingerprints, while the officer checked that the front-door locks had not been forced, thereby proving that the burglar had either used a master key or climbed in over the balcony. There was no trace of fingerprints, but the inspector found a dirty red bundle that contained jewelry the old lady said was not hers. So this apartment was apparently not the burglar's first stop that day, and he must have been disturbed. The inspector advised her not to stay alone for a few nights. The old lady thought he was a fussy creature, but since the manager agreed with him, she called her daughter and asked for her help with what she called a little spot of bother.
